correctness.rationale: For the stated a+b>=3, arm-state case analysis is complete: when the hub is black a one-black long arm is uniquely WWB and forces all other first vertices black; when white, every three-edge arm costs two black vertices and at least one BBW pattern is necessary at the optimum. The sharp lower bounds, construction lists and disjoint counts prove the claim at all integer parameters. A standalone checker independently enumerated all subsets on 24 small profiles and compared complete minimizer families, then checked 66549 constructions in 78 larger profiles. Finite tests are corroborative rather than proof.

originality.rationale: The nontrivial new component is the complete enumeration and classification. General tree matching theorems cover the numerical minimum only; the 2022 enumeration paper explicitly asks to count minimum sets in trees and treats other families. Comparison with nearby published records yields no implication to the stated count. The potentially related 2024 all-size polynomial paper was inaccessible beyond its abstract and is a residual risk, not asserted absent.

value.rationale: A natural two-parameter spider subclass solves a concrete portion of the prior stated problem of enumerating tree optima. The complete structural classification explains a sharp counting transition: with a long arm present, arbitrarily many added two-edge arms do not change optimum multiplicity, while with only short arms multiplicity is exponential in their number plus a correction. This is more than a numerical minimum recomputation or a parameter relabeling and provides a local-pattern method for other trees.
